reference_sql:
WITH starts AS (
  -- one row per session_start event from 8 to 15 December 2025
  SELECT event_date, user_pseudo_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_id')[1].value.int_value AS ga_session_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_number')[1].value.int_value AS ga_session_number
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'session_start'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251208' AND '20251215'
)
SELECT event_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ga_session_number = 1 THEN user_pseudo_id || '-' || CAST(ga_session_id AS VARCHAR) END) AS first_sessions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ga_session_number > 1 THEN user_pseudo_id || '-' || CAST(ga_session_id AS VARCHAR) END) AS returning_sessions
FROM starts
GROUP BY event_date
alternatives:
WITH starts AS (
  -- one row per session_start event with both IDs from 8 to 15 December 2025
  SELECT event_date,
    [p.value.int_value FOR p IN event_params IF p.key = 'ga_session_number'][1] AS ga_session_number
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'session_start'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251208' AND '20251215'
    AND user_pseudo_id IS NOT NULL
    AND [p.value.int_value FOR p IN event_params IF p.key = 'ga_session_id'][1] IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT event_date,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ga_session_number = 1) AS first_sessions,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ga_session_number > 1) AS returning_sessions
FROM starts
GROUP BY event_date

WITH sessions AS (
  -- one row per session (user_pseudo_id and ga_session_id) that started from 8 to 15 December 2025
  SELECT DISTINCT event_date, user_pseudo_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_id')[1].value.int_value AS ga_session_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_number')[1].value.int_value AS ga_session_number
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'session_start'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251208' AND '20251215'
)
SELECT event_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ga_session_number = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_sessions,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ga_session_number > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS returning_sessions
FROM sessions
WHERE user_pseudo_id IS NOT NULL AND ga_session_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY event_date

other_way.tradeoff: Counting session_start rows with FILTER is shorter, and right here because each session has exactly one session_start.

solver.query:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT event_date, user_pseudo_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_id')[1].value.int_value AS sid,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'ga_session_number')[1].value.int_value AS num
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'session_start' AND event_date BETWEEN '20251208' AND '20251215'
)
SELECT event_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN num = 1 THEN (user_pseudo_id, sid) END) AS first_sessions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN num > 1 THEN (user_pseudo_id, sid) END) AS returning_sessions
FROM s WHERE user_pseudo_id IS NOT NULL AND sid IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY event_date
